on the roof of a large industrial building on the north side of NC Hwy 5.

set back behind a rail line. Web search confirmed the site as Pactiv Corporation
(formerly International Tray Pads), an absorbent products / foam tray-pad
converting plant, phone (910) 944-1800 — consistent with the roster facility type.
Locked center on the building footprint at 35.138550, -79.437750.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Driveway runs directly from NC Hwy 5 across a CSX-type rail spur into the property with no barrier arm, sliding gate, or checkpoint. Confirmed via 2024-05 Street View at the driveway entrance.

fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Driveway crosses the rail line then runs ~120 m before reaching the dock apron - room for a 3+ truck queue.

fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town light-industrial corridor on NC Hwy 5 in Aberdeen, surrounded by pine woods - Rural.

sites.name: Pactiv Evergreen - Canandaigua NY
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster coordinate (42.903839, -77.301317) lands on the south end of a very
large Pactiv industrial campus on North Street, NW of Canandaigua, NY. Web
search confirmed Pactiv LLC operates a plastics/foam food-packaging plant at
5250 North Street (the campus has been in continuous operation since 1966 and
is Ontario County's largest private employer, >700 employees). Satellite probes
from z15 down to z19 mapped the full campus: a cluster of dark-roof
manufacturing buildings on the east side (the plant — idx 2) plus several
tan-roof warehouse/distribution buildings to the west, all inside one
contiguous fenced and gated property. Note: the idx 3 CTC Distribution Center
(2480 Sommers Drive) carries the ZIP+4 14424-5250 — it is the warehouse/DC
half of this same campus.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Confirmed in Street View (2016-09) at the campus south entrance ~42.9028,-77.3030: a black-and-white striped barrier arm spans the truck lane, flanked by two sliding chain-link gates and STOP signs. Perimeter chain-link fencing rings the whole property. This is the single shared gate for the whole Pactiv Canandaigua campus.
fieldNotes.guardShack: A small flat-roof booth sits immediately left of the gate (windowed on multiple sides, ~1-2 vehicle footprint, set beside the gate lane). It carries an 'Adecco' staffing-agency sign and a US flag pole — it is the staffed check-in booth at the gate.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — a guard booth is present. A 'Pick Up Phone For Directions' call-box kiosk also sits at the gate as a secondary check-in aid, but the booth itself is the primary staffed control.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Broad paved apron and internal access road inside the gate before the trailer yards / dock banks gives ample internal queue room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The gate-to-dock approach runs several hundred metres up the campus access road; can hold well over 3 trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide gate apron with two sliding-gate bays plus the barrier arm; ample paved width to add a dedicated express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Plant complex (dark-roof eastern buildings): a dock apron with ~6-8 doors on the SW plant face plus additional doors along the long warehouse-adjacent faces; estimate ~40 doors campus-wide. Low-confidence overhead count.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive marked trailer drop yards on the west and central campus hold well over 100 parked trailers in long rows — clearly 50+ band.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Multiple distinct dock banks on different building faces across the campus (plant SW face vs. warehouse faces) imply physically separate ship/receive flows; functional split not verifiable from imagery.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: True — large campus of 6+ connected/adjacent large buildings: the dark-roof manufacturing plant complex plus several tan-roof warehouse/distribution buildings.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage lots full of parked trailers occupy much of the west campus, separate from active dock staging.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail spur enters the campus from the NE, curving down the east property edge into the plant; rail cars visible parked on the spur in imagery.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: North Street industrial corridor on the NW edge of Canandaigua (a small NY town); campus is bordered by woods, farm fields and a retention pond. Edge-of-town / rural setting.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~220 trailers counted across the visible drop-yard rows; honest estimate from overhead imagery.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Derived from the campus perimeter box (~145 acres); the gated property is large with substantial wooded buffer.

fieldNotes.dropArea: Trailer drop/parking lots around the east warehouse and along the rail side hold an estimated 25-50 parked trailers; honest overhead estimate.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock banks on different building faces (east warehouse dock bank vs. west/rail-side plant docks) imply physically separate ship/receive flows; functional split not verifiable from imagery.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: True — a multi-building manufacturing campus: a large warehouse building plus several connected manufacturing buildings on the same fenced property.

The plant address is 4501 E. Business State Highway 31 — the Business

32.0987, -96.4206, on the north side of the E State Highway 31 service

- A long L-shaped white metal manufacturing building with a row of
  resin storage silos along the highway frontage — silos are diagnostic of

fieldNotes.location: Roster geocode (32.075885,-96.397359, RANGE_INTERPOLATED) was wrong — it placed the point ~5 km SE in open woodland/farmland on the SH-31 bypass (confirmed empty by satellite z14-z17 and Street View, captured 2024-02). Address is '4501 E. Business State Highway 31' (Business 31, not the bypass). The Pactiv plant was positively re-located at 32.0987,-96.4206 on the north side of the E State Highway 31 service road: a fully fenced plastics manufacturing complex with a long L-shaped white metal manufacturing building, a row of resin storage silos along the frontage (diagnostic of a plastics/thermoforming plant — confirmed in Street View 2024-02), a brick office building, and an extensive trailer drop yard. Plant built ~1999, ~500 employees, makes cups/lids/to-go containers/breakfast trays (corsicanadailysun, Corsicana Chamber).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Property is fully enclosed by chain-link perimeter fence (visible in satellite and behind the highway hedge in Street View). A single access driveway connects the yard to the E SH-31 service road at the NE corner — a controlled pinch-point. truckGate = true.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed guard booth structure is visible at the entrance in any satellite view (z18-z20). Entrance is a fenced driveway opening. Street View of the entrance itself is obscured by a tall hedge along the highway, so a small booth cannot be 100% excluded — listed uncertain. Best read: no guard shack.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present, no visible guard booth -> remoteGs = true (kiosk / call-box / app check-in implied). Medium confidence given hedge obstruction.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Large dedicated trailer-storage lot on the west/southwest side of the manufacturing building — dozens of trailers parked in organized rows (visible at z18-z20). Clear dedicated drop yard.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+ — counted roughly 80-100 parked trailers/storage units across the west yard rows in z18/z19 imagery.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Dock doors run along the south/southwest face of the manufacturing building facing the yard; estimated ~20-25 doors. Low-confidence count — roof shadow and trailer occlusion. Banded 10-25.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The entrance driveway runs a long distance from the SH-31 service road across a deep paved apron into the yard — ample stacking room for 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide unfenced paved aprons at the entrance and inside the yard; room to add bypass lanes.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Main manufacturing building plus a separate brick office building and at least one ancillary structure; ~3. The dense piping/tank complex immediately to the southwest is a SEPARATE property (a legacy Corsicana oil/asphalt terminal), not part of the Pactiv site.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: East edge of Corsicana along the SH-31 corridor; open farmland and scattered industrial parcels around. Edge-of-town / rural.
